 Oral Order

Petitioner is before this Court calling in question proceedings in C.C.No.435/2024, pending before the learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bengaluru Rural District, Bengaluru, for the offences under Sections 506, 498A, 504 and 323 of the IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.

entities.text: Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bengaluru Rural District, Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Learned counsel for the petitioner and respondent No.2, in unison submit that the parties to the lis have settled their matrimonial dispute among themselves and are living together happily.
The parties have filed a joint memo in this regard seeking permission to compound the offences before this Court.
One of the conditions of the settlement recognizes the closure of the present proceedings.

3. The joint memo filed by the parties to the lis reads as follows:
"JOINT MEMO FILED BY THE PETITIONER AND RESPONDENT NO.2 NC:
2026:KHC:278 HC-KAR The Petitioner and Respondent No.2 herein most humbly submit as under:
1. The Petitioners and Respondent No.2 at the intervention of elders, friends and well wishes have amicably settled all their disputes amongst themselves.
2. The Petitioner and Respondent No.2 herein along with their minor Son Yashith,
Aged about 3 years, are living together happily since from the past one year without any problem or complaints.
3. In view of the above, the Respondent No.2 herein does not have any objection in quashing the Criminal Case in C.C. No.435/2024 for the offence punishable under Sections 506, 498A, 504 and 323 of I.P.C. R/w.
Sections 3 and 4 of D.P. Act pending against the Petitioner herein on the file of the learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bengaluru Rural District at Bengaluru.

entities.text: Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bengaluru Rural District at Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: WHEREFORE, this Hon'ble Court be pleased to quash the Criminal Case in C.C. No.435/2024 for the offence punishable under Sections 506, 498A, 504 and 323 of I.P.C. R/w. Sections 3 and 4 of D.P. Act pending against the Petitioner herein on the file of the learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bengaluru Rural District at Bengaluru, in the interest of justice and equity."

In the light of the afore-quoted joint memo of the parties and the fact that they are living together happily,
though the offences alleged against the petitioner in the case at hand inter alia is the one punishable under Section 498A of the IPC, I deem it appropriate to accept the joint memo and permit them NC:
2026:KHC:278 HC-KAR to compound the offences, as the allegations are not against the State.

4. For the aforesaid reasons, I pass the following:
ORDER Mr. Bhuvanesh K J vs State By Avalahally Police Station on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101211021/
